PC: Elicit appropriate history (key question: any history of choking/gagging/coughing spell in the past few weeks?).
Perform pertinent physical exam (key skill: listen for stridor or asymmetric breath sounds).
Correctly and efficiently assemble bronchoscope (within 2 minutes is appropriate, with selection of appropriate optical tool for removal).
Successfully perform direct laryngoscopy (protect maxilla, apply topical lidocaine to prevent laryngospasm)

Recognize and appropriately respond to laryngospasm (communicate with team, stop surgical stimulation, apply positive pressure ventilation, consider pharmacologic treatment with propofol or short-acting paralytic, topicalize true vocal cords if this has not already been done to prevent recurrence with further manipulation).
Appropriately manage desaturation (removal of optical apparatus to allow full diameter of ventilating bronchoscope for gas exchange).
Successfully retrieve foreign body from trachea
MK: Order and appropriately interpret radiographic studies (inspiratory/expiratory films, lateral decubitus films, or airway fluoroscopy).
SBP: Return patient to anesthesia for recovery
ICS: Discuss appropriate anesthetic management plan with anesthesia before going to the operating room (inhalant induction under spontaneous ventilation).
